sections.heading: Resources Built From Real Consulting Work
paragraphs: Every resource on this page comes out of work Traction Outsourcing has done inside real Nigerian businesses — the patterns we see repeated in HR audits, leadership training, and corporate restructuring engagements across Nigeria and Africa.

Some of what you'll find here is free: practical documents built for HR teams, founders, and executives who want a faster starting point. Others, like the book below, are paid resources for readers who want a deeper, more personal take.

sections.title: Nigerian Bosses Are Bad
sections.subtitle: A Short Book on Perspective, Pressure, and the People Who Lead Us
blurb_paragraphs: Somewhere in Lagos tonight, somebody is typing a resignation letter at 11 p.m. They will save it in drafts. They will not send it, because rent does not care how you feel about your Oga, and neither does the landlord who is already asking for next quarter before this one has ended.

If you have worked under a Nigerian boss, you have said it at least once. Maybe under your breath in the office toilet. Maybe into your phone on the drive home. "This one is wicked." "That woman does not have human blood." "How can somebody treat people like this?"
sections.sample_text:
Chapter Two
The Boss Who Changes Her Mind Every Monday

Tunde had a private nickname for his CEO within six months of joining the fintech in Yaba. He called her NEPA. Her instructions took light like PHCN, here now, gone before you'd finished adjusting to it.

The product roadmap that was locked on Monday was scrapped by Wednesday. A payment-processor deal he'd spent three weeks negotiating died two days before signing, killed by a text that said only, it's not the right time anymore. He'd stay up getting a set of wireframes exactly right, proud of the work, and two days later learn none of it would ship.

There is a version of this story where Amaka is simply indecisive, a founder who talks a confident game in pitch decks and falls apart the moment a real decision needs holding. That version isn't entirely wrong.

It also isn't the whole picture. Amaka runs a fintech company inside a regulatory environment where the Central Bank can issue a circular on a Tuesday morning that makes Monday's entire business model illegal by lunchtime. Her cloud…
